title: Binary Tree Lowest Common Ancestor
problem: In a family lineage tracking system, users often need to understand the kinship between two members. Your task: given the complete family tree tree (with node ids and parent-child edges), for any specified members p and q, compute the deepest common ancestor node of the two, and return its id as a string.
strategy: DFS returns whether the current subtree contains p or q; when both left and right subtrees contain a target, the current node is the LCA.
learning_objectives: Understand the state changes of whether the current subtree contains p or q during DFS recursion.
Based on the recursive backtracking order, predict which node will be processed next.
Use the invariant 'if both left and right subtrees return non-null, then the current node is the LCA' to verify the algorithm's correctness.

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Correct! You accurately tracked the recursive order.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Take a look at the changes in call_stack in the trace to see which node will be pushed next.
interaction_tasks.oracle: Judge based on the node id recorded in the trace for the next step.
interaction_tasks.prompt: The current recursive node is 5, the left child call returned None, which node will be processed next?
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Highlight the node that will be processed next and display the expected action.

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Exactly! Both left and right hit, so the current node is the LCA.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Review: When both left and right subtrees have targets, what role does the current node play?
interaction_tasks.oracle: The return value should be node 2, and it is the LCA of 7 and 4.
interaction_tasks.prompt: When processing node 2 recursively, the left child returned 7 and the right child returned 4. What invariant should the return value of node 2 satisfy at this point?
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Highlight node 2 and its left and right child return values in the tree view.

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Great! You discovered that when p is an ancestor of q, the LCA is p.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Check the relationship between p and q: Is 6 a child node of 5?
interaction_tasks.oracle: Expected LCA should be 5, because 5 itself is the ancestor of 6.
interaction_tasks.prompt: If the tree structure remains unchanged, change q to 6 while keeping p as 5, what node will the LCA become?
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Allow students to drag to modify the values of p or q and observe the change in LCA.

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Perfect! This is exactly the core judgment logic of LCA.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Think about it: At this point, node 3's left and right subtrees each contain one target, so who is the common ancestor of these two targets?
interaction_tasks.oracle: Because both left and right subtrees contain one target each, according to the algorithm logic, the current node is the lowest common ancestor.
interaction_tasks.prompt: In the recursion at node 3, the left child (5) returned 5 and the right child (1) returned 1. Why does the final answer become 3?
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Animate recursive backtracking and flash a marker on node 3 when both subtrees turn green.
